chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Habib al-Khasha'i, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'I wish to marry a woman, but my parents desire another for me.' He said, 'Marry the one you desire, and leave the one your parents desire.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when a man wants to marry a woman his parents do not approve of?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of individual autonomy in marital choice, ruling that the suitor's personal preference (*hawiyah*) takes precedence over parental wishes. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that while respecting parents is obligatory, it does not extend to overriding the spouse's consent or choice in marriage, thereby preventing potential discord (*fitnah*) that may arise from forced unions.
